title: Asymmetric arm assignment
abstract: A synthetic conditional extension that assigns distinct protective roles to the two RNA arms and remains visible as a separate research object even though it has no dedicated report file.
disposition_reason: The object remains plausible but depends on evidence that the two arms occupy distinguishable functional roles.
nearest_prior_art: Asymmetric RNA architecture concepts without this synthetic arm-specific causal assignment.
strongest_reason: It produces a directional prediction that symmetry controls cannot explain.
weakest_causal_edge: Arm-specific functional exposure has not been established.
pairwise_summary: Not pairwise-ranked in this focused run.
reviewer_disagreement: The primary disagreement concerns whether the arm roles are physically separable.
reviewer_critiques: Matched arm swaps are required to avoid sequence-composition confounding.
reentry_condition: Advance after an arm-swap contrast shows a directional effect at matched abundance.
scientific_summary: Distinct arm assignments could make the protective architecture directional rather than symmetric.
causal_mechanism: One arm would preferentially preserve the upstream assembly state while the other protects the downstream intermediate.
evidence_basis: Synthetic mechanistic extrapolation with no complete-architecture validation.
next_discriminating_experiment: Run matched arm-swap and symmetry controls while holding composition and bulk abundance constant.
